analysis:
Examined the two base_text units (lines 624-1505) of ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift. They are the unchanged tail of the inference task body: the encrypted response path, cache receipts, usage/billing floors and terminal sends. The PR changes are in other ranges (head lines 193-194, 346-351, 365, 398-410, 553-557). I saw only a truncated patch excerpt, so the new `workFIFOGate` parameter and the `decodeInboundChatRequest` / `inbound.extensions` change are not fully visible.

In the visible base text I found no regression relevant to T-008, T-041, A-001 or A-003. Encryption failure still fails closed: `emitSSE` (lines 801-836) sends an `.encryptionFailure` terminal and aborts without emitting plaintext. Response-key setup failure at lines 776-794 is also fail-closed. Cache scope is still taken from `remoteCache.scope`/`cacheScope`, which are coordinator-authored. Cache result usage is reported only when the scope is non-nil (line 1468). The Super owner path uses `remoteCache.scope` and emits no cache receipts. Logging of Jinja failures omits message content (lines 1015-1028).

Open items for later passes: (1) how the head side uses `inbound.extensions` and `templateControls`, and whether the single-parse path still treats cache scope/salt as coordinator-authored and ignores caller-supplied `prompt_cache_key`/`user` (T-041). (2) Where `workFIFOGate` is acquired and released on every terminal path, including cancel and early-reject, since an unreleased gate could cause a DoS. (3) Whether `decodeInboundChatRequest` reads body extensions that could alter trusted control fields (the `templateControls` comes from authenticated plaintext). The head-side changed ranges (346-351, 398-410, 553-557) were not supplied, so I cannot conclude these are safe.
